Mean C_vol is the arithmetic mean of the three native volumetric readings at each group; add exactly 273.15 for kelvin. The computed replicate sample SD is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)) and is a separate TabulatedOnly statistic, not a confidence interval or calibration uncertainty. Extra computed digits represent arithmetic, not increased measurement resolution. Linear mean C_vol(T) and published Cp(T) interpolation is an authored approximation between the four groups with no measured interpolation-error bound or extrapolation. Native C_vol(T) needs no independent density(T).

The files PVC_Density_Wet_R1.csv, PVC_Density_Wet_R2.csv, PVC_Density_Wet_R3.csv report densities 1385,1388,1391 kg/m3, masses 182.3,181.4,180.4 g and volumes 131.6,130.7,129.7 cm3, respectively. The primary reduction uses the arithmetic mean of the reported rounded density column, 1388 kg/m3; recomputing mass/volume would change its inputs. Density test temperature is unspecified. Reference-normalization-density retains this algebraic input without temperature validity and is not a constant bulk-density law or density measured at every thermal knot.

FSRI divides each mean native C_vol by the common mean reported density and rounds to whole J/(kg K), yielding 972,1020,1042,1076 at 10,20,30,40 degC. Its reported standard deviations 6,15,11,11 J/(kg K) are the native volume-capacity sample SD divided by that same mean density, rounded to whole units. Density scatter, calibration uncertainty and covariance are not propagated. Cp, C_vol and normalization density are algebraically related, not independent measurements. The published rounded Cp and SD values are retained exactly.

column5: Thermal-conductivity requires mean-test-temperature-as-local-model=1. This explicitly accepts substituting the measured apparent through-thickness conductivity at a finite nominal 20 K plate difference for a local conductivity at the same numerical temperature. It is an engineering approximation, not deconvolution of the plate temperatures or a new point measurement. Apparent-thermal-conductivity separately retains its native test-mean-temperature axis.
